A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WonderWorld and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. The complete supplied material, including v3's supplementary Sections A–D, supports reliable comparison and matching of relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated scenes, qualitative comparisons, and measured generation times in Section 4 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v3 reports original generation times, image-quality measurements, human preferences, and ablation outcomes in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: FGS and the existing three-layer generation are consolidated as FLAGS. Surfel construction, back-to-front optimization, optimized parameters, loss, 100 iterations, and depth guidance are retained. Nonzero surfel thickness was already disclosed in v1, and the scale coefficient is equivalently reparameterized. Added pseudocode and implementation details do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 Figure 1 adds two casual-walk camera trajectories to the panoramic demonstrations, extending the demonstrated exploration scenarios. Real and synthetic city, campus, nature, and fantasy imagery already appear in v1; most supplementary examples retain this coverage.

E2.justification: Text2Room changes from a related-work citation in v1 to an evaluated comparator in v3's timing, visual, quality-score, and human comparisons. WonderJourney and LucidDreamer remain, while the existing 3DGS/Mip-Splatting comparison is retained within the geometry ablation.

E3.justification: v1's qualitative comparison used nine WonderWorld scenes, up to four WonderJourney scenes, and one LucidDreamer scene. v3 reports seven scenes for each of four inputs, shared panoramic paths/prompts with reduced baseline camera distances, nine-view scoring, and randomized 2AFC surveys with 204 participants per comparison. Its geometry ablation additionally matches generation-view PSNR.

E4.justification: v3 extends v1's qualitative initialization and depth-guidance comparisons into a quantitative three-component ablation suite in Table 4. It adds a single-layer control testing whether layering fills occluded regions, illustrated in Figure 7. The earlier initialization and guidance illustrations are retained or reformatted rather than newly introduced analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new human-study participant count concerns sample size, and preference percentages are point results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 add quality, preference, and ablation results, including CLIP scores of 29.47 for WonderWorld versus 27.34 for WonderJourney. Human preferences favor WonderWorld by 98.5%, 98.6%, and 98.0% against WonderJourney, LucidDreamer, and Text2Room, respectively. Text2Room's 766.9-second runtime is added; existing timing values remain unchanged. These are newly reported evaluations, not demonstrated same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the scale-initialization reasoning: v1 uses proportionality to a Nyquist interval, while v3 explicitly derives scales by relating surface sampling frequency to Gaussian bandwidth. This is a limited mathematical refinement with equivalent effective initialization; no theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central single-image, user-controlled, sub-10-second generation claim remains. v3 narrows the abstract and formulation's emphasis from potentially infinite virtual worlds to connected scenes, and its conclusion explicitly frames the system as scene prototyping.

C2.justification: v3 replaces low surfel density as the principal stated limitation with a fundamental applicability restriction: generated surfaces face forward, preventing exploration behind objects. It explicitly presents WonderWorld as a prototype rather than a complete solution, while retaining detailed-object failures. It also adds an explanation linking Text2Room's outdoor failures to indoor training.

D1.justification: v3 adds three algorithms, the structured GPT-4 prompt and GPT-4V captioning details, opacity initialization, 512×512 resolution, 960-pixel focal lengths, and the 0.6 visibility threshold. Supplementary Sections C–D also explain ground-depth calculation and survey implementation. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; code release remains prospective.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to single-image novel-view representations, layered depth images, additional scene generators, and guidance methods. v3 explicitly connects FLAGS to layered depth images and radiance fields and adds positioning against methods such as BlockFusion and InstantSplat. This exceeds bibliographic or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. v3 combines the surfel and layer-generation sections under FLAGS, adds an explicit contribution list, reorganizes experiments, and creates supplementary Sections A–D for algorithms, details, and qualitative material.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the teaser and framework diagrams, revises the scale illustration, splits and updates baseline comparisons, and adds quality, preference, and ablation tables plus algorithm displays. Many panoramic examples and the timing breakdown move to the supplement; these relocations are distinguishable from genuinely new displays.

improvement.justification: v1 supports scene quality mainly through illustrations. v3 adds quantitative comparisons, human preferences, and component ablations, substantially strengthening that evidence. Detailed implementation documentation and explicit viewpoint restrictions also improve reproducibility and claim calibration. Evaluation on only four inputs, adjusted baseline camera distances, and absent uncertainty reporting still limit validation, but the overall evidential and explanatory gains are substantial.
